content.comment_body: Hello, I've installed [product_name] version [version_no], added a slider component and want to link it to a Modbus-read variable. In the Variable > Block Type section, I see AI, AQ, AM, VB, VD, VW, but I need to reference data from a HOLDING REGISTER. I'm using [product_name] version [version_no], configured as Modbus master communicating with a remote slave. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Which [product_name] exactly do you have? Please provide the full [article_no] and firmware [version_no]. Also, what is the size of the Modbus register—1 or 2 registers? What is the data type: Integer, Double Integer, or Real?

Hello, A Modbus holding register typically contains integer values. Within [product_name], you need to use VW. The VW address should be set up in the Modbus data table for the holding register. Direct addressing isn't possible because [product_name] doesn't know your communication setup or the configured address range. Hope this clarifies things.

Thanks for your responses. I don't have the device at the moment—just the simulator. The general steps should be: In [product_name] comfort: - Go to Tools > Ethernet > create Modbus client connection - Go to Tools > Parameter VM mapping In [product_name]: - Global config > Tag Table > set the VM previously defined
If you would like my support, please answer the questions I previously asked.

Hi, apologies for the delay. The [product_name] is [product_name] with firmware [version_no]. It's acting as a Modbus TCP/IP server reading 2 holding registers as integers; one register serves as the set point, the other displays the actual value. I've added the addresses, but no data seems to be coming through. Is there a way to debug this? [IMAGE]

Can you specify which Modbus device you're using (manufacturer and type)? Do you have a table of register addresses? Are you certain that unit ID 255 is correct? With [product_name], register addresses start at 1 instead of 0. Does your Modbus device begin numbering at 0 or 1? If it starts at 0, you need to offset the addresses in [product_name].

I've resolved the address issue, thank you. The mapping differs across clients—reading address 1 elsewhere corresponds to address 2 in [product_name]. However, if I include additional addresses that do not exist, all data views disappear, including correct data. How can I identify problematic addresses or check the connection status?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are attempting to integrate [product_name] with a [product_name] device using Modbus protocol for visualizing holding register data. They face challenges in aligning interface elements with accurate Modbus addressing in [product_name], and if an invalid address is configured, all data visualization disappears, making debugging more complex.
analysis.user_expectations: Users desire straightforward mapping of Modbus holding registers in [product_name], robust error handling, and clear diagnostic feedback to identify incorrect addresses or communication issues easily.
